vectorised_host.note: worker threads = min(num_envs, performance-core count); this M4 has 4 P + 6 E cores

plateau.finding: throughput saturates at ~18.5k from 2 envs upward even though 4 cores are busy: per-core throughput halves between 2 and 4 envs
plateau.discriminating_experiment: 4 SEPARATE processes with 1 env each total 33,522 SPS (9442+8736+7793+7551); one process with 4 envs gets 18,493
plateau.conclusion: the cap is INTRA-PROCESS, not the machine. The vectorised host reaches ~55% of what the same cores deliver across processes. Likely the per-step spin barrier (it waits for the slowest shard, and Python dispatches every step) and/or shared-cache pressure from four ~64KB per-env working sets on the M4's single P-core cluster.
plateau.not_fixed: fixing it means changing native/qjs/qjs_vec_host.cpp, which FIRST_PERSON_PLAN.md authorises only for the voxel bindings. Recorded, not changed.
plateau.same_family_as: the glibc arena lock convoys in the async AOT host, fixed there by env pinning
